title: When not to play
translation: Someone once told me: "When a gambler has been losing badly and he's about to bet everything he has left, don't play against him. That's the moment his luck turns, and he'll win again and again. A good gambler knows when that moment has come."
original: 「{博奕|ばくち}の{負|ま}け{極|きは}まりて、{残|のこ}りなくうち{入|い}れむとせむに、{逢|あ}ひては{打|う}つべからず。
{立|た}ち{帰|かへ}りつづけて{勝|か}つべき{時|とき}の{至|いた}れると{知|し}るべし。
その{時|とき}を{知|し}るを、よき{博奕|ばくち}といふなり。」と、あるもの{申|まう}しき。
literal: 'When someone's losses at gambling have reached the extreme and he is about to stake everything that is left, you must not face him and play.
You should know that the time has come when (his luck) turns back and he will win in a row.
Knowing that time is what is called a good gambler', someone said.

notes.text: {博奕|ばくち}: gambling, and also a gambler, as in the last sentence. In Kenkō's time the usual games were played with dice, such as sugoroku, a board game played for stakes.

notes.quote: 残りなくうち入れむとせむに
notes.text: うち{入|い}る: 'to put in, to stake'. むとす: 'to be about to'. The second む makes it a general case: 'whenever someone is about to…'.

notes.quote: 逢ひては打つべからず
notes.text: {逢|あ}ふ: here 'to face as an opponent'. {打|う}つ is the verb for playing dice or board games, still used for {博打|ばくち}を{打|う}つ.

notes.quote: 立ち帰りつづけて勝つべき
notes.text: {立|た}ち{帰|かへ}る: 'to come back, to turn round'. His luck turns, and he wins several times in a row.
き: Kenkō heard it himself. The whole section is one quoted piece of advice, and he adds nothing to it.
